meta.purpose: Within-stream ordered-pair relatedness: modified-file overlap, gold-patch and problem-statement TF-IDF cosines, precomputed for every pair (a before b) in each canonical chronological stream; plus every ordered cross-repo pair of each shipped run-order under the separate run_orders map.

metrics.pos_a: 1-based position of a; canonical-stream position in streams entries, run-order position in run_orders entries
metrics.pos_b: 1-based position of b; same convention as pos_a
metrics.shared_files: modified-file paths (regex over 'diff --git a/... b/' in gold patches) shared by both tasks
metrics.patch_cosine: TF-IDF cosine of gold patches; tokens = camelCase-split identifiers (>=2 chars; snake_case and all-caps runs kept whole), terms in >=3 docs, sublinear tf, natural-ln idf
metrics.problem_cosine: TF-IDF cosine of the two problem statements, used verbatim; same token/term/tf/idf spec as patch_cosine but a separate matrix over the 500 statements — idf never mixes with the patch corpus
metrics.problem_similar_threshold: nearest-rank p75 of the entry's pair problem_cosine values (computed on the shipped 4 dp values, stored rounded to 4 dp); omitted when the entry has no pairs. A pair is problem-similar iff problem_cosine >= threshold, both as shipped 4 dp values
metrics.quadrant: opportunity = problem-similar and relation_strength >= 2; trap = problem-similar and relation_strength == 0; deep_transfer = problem-dissimilar and relation_strength >= 2; neutral = everything else (test-file-only overlap never leaves neutral)
metrics.shared_test_files: test-patch modified-file paths shared by both tasks (same diff --git regex as gold patches); present only when non-empty
metrics.shared_symbols: symbols from gold-patch hunk headers (@@ ... @@ def/class/function name) that both patches touch in the same file; present only when non-empty
metrics.relation_strength: strongest gold-evidence grade: 3 same symbol in a shared file > 2 shared gold file > 1 shared test file only > 0 unrelated
metrics.days_between: created_at(b) - created_at(a) in days, rounded to 4 dp; >= 0 everywhere (chronology is never inverted)
metrics.problem_margin: round(problem_cosine - problem_similar_threshold, 4); >= 0 iff problem-similar under the pinned rule. A conditioning convenience, never a delivery predictor; location-normalized only — equal margins are not equal extremity across streams
metrics.shared_problem_identifiers: code identifiers in both problem statements under the pinned regex classes (URLs stripped first; backtick-span parts kept when identifier-shaped — >= 3 chars with an underscore or a non-initial uppercase — unless the span is a slash path, which emits the whole path only; dotted/slash paths whole; identifier-shaped tokens anywhere), lowercased/deduplicated/sorted; present only when non-empty
metrics.shared_problem_identifier_count: len(shared_problem_identifiers); present on every record, 0 where the list is absent
metrics.tasks_with_earlier_file_overlap: tasks having >=1 strictly earlier same-repo task sharing a gold file
metrics.tasks_with_earlier_relation: tasks having >=1 strictly earlier same-repo task at relation_strength >= 1
metrics.tasks_with_earlier_opportunity: tasks having >=1 strictly earlier same-repo pair labeled opportunity
metrics.tasks_with_earlier_trap: tasks having >=1 strictly earlier same-repo pair labeled trap
metrics.tasks_with_earlier_deep_transfer: tasks having >=1 strictly earlier same-repo pair labeled deep_transfer
metrics.tasks_with_earlier_cross_repo: (run_orders entries) tasks having >=1 earlier task from a different repo in that run-order

meta.run_orders: One entry per shipped run-order file (the 4 neighbor folders and the repo-interference streams), keyed by the file's rel path, holding every ordered cross-repo pair (a before b in that run-order). Cross-repo records carry relation_strength 0 / shared_file_count 0 / file_jaccard 0.0 and omit quadrant (thresholds are per canonical stream; a cross-repo quadrant would collapse to trap/neutral). Same-repo pairs are never duplicated here — join them from the canonical entries via (a, b), with canonical positions. Cores ship no entry: a core's pairs are a subset of its canonical stream's records.
analyses: missed-recall opportunities (high-overlap pair with no memory injection at b)
injudge verdict rates conditioned on pair relatedness or quadrant
meta.rule: conditions aggregates and flags opportunities — never a verdict source; verdicts derive from subsequent influence in injudge.
